packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 13 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (first reader)

EXPOSURE / RULES STATEMENT
- Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of the work or author. I make none here.
- One step beyond the stated rules: image-002 to image-005 show their text upside down AND mirror-reversed.
  To read them I made temporary flipped copies (vertical flip) of those four tiles in a scratch
  directory and viewed the copies. No other file, directory, catalogue, web page or search tool was used.
  I did not read packet.json.

CONVENTIONS
- ] or [ at a line end = text cut by the edge of the strip (true of EVERY line in this packet).
- (..) = proposed expansion; ? after a word = uncertain reading; [..] = letters hidden under the
  sewing thread / gutter line or abraded; [illegible] = nothing recoverable.
- Line numbers count from the top of the named image, EXCEPT for image-002..005 (see strip 1).
  Counts are approximate to +-1 because tiles start mid-line.
- Abbreviation marks are kept where I could see them: q̄, ē, n̄, ꝑ, ꝓ, ꝰ, ⁊ (Tironian et), ÷ (est), ; (-us/-et/-que sign).

=====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)
=====================================================================
Observations
- The packet shows eight narrow vertical parchment strips, each mounted in the gutter of a later
  paper book (stitching thread and a fold line run down several of them). Overviews: image-001,
  006, 011, 016, 021, 026, 031, 036. Each overview is followed by four overlapping tiles.
- Each strip is roughly one to three words wide and about 45-60 written lines tall. No strip shows
  a full line, a column edge with margin on both sides, a running title, or a rubric.
- Script: a small, heavily abbreviated book hand in brown-black ink, upright, with many suspension
  strokes and superscript letters. Line spacing is tight.
- Brown ink underlining of individual words or line-segments occurs repeatedly (noted per line below).
- Tiny interlinear additions above the line occur on several strips (image-023, 025, 028-030, 032-035, 038),
  in a smaller hand or the same hand at reduced size.
- Red marks on the HOST paper beside the strips (not on the parchment): image-001/002-005 (four red
  marks), image-006/008-010 (red marks at left), image-011/014-015, image-016-020, image-024 (". IA ."),
  image-029 ("di . IA" or similar), image-033 and 038. They look like letter/number sigla; I cannot
  read them securely and they are cropped.
- image-017/018: a second, smaller parchment fragment lies to the left of the main strip, with a few
  letters and red ink of its own.
- image-027..030 and image-032: the strip is two-ply or folded; a thin inner sliver at the left
  carries one or two letters per line that do not obviously continue the main sliver.
- No enlarged or decorated initials visible. One capital-like letter opens image-027 line 1.

Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- The underlined words could be lemmata or quoted words inside running prose commentary, and the
  interlinear notes could be glosses; the crop is too tight to confirm either.
- Strip 1 (image-001..005) is seen reversed and inverted, i.e. probably the glued/other face seen
  through, or a strip mounted head-down and photographed from behind.
- Whether the eight strips come from one leaf, and in what order, cannot be decided from these crops.

Areas selected: every tile of every strip was read line by line (there is no connected prose to
select; each line preserves only a word or two). Areas left unread: lower half of image-040 and
image-039 lines 17 onward (abraded), the small left fragment in image-017/018, the inner sliver in
image-027..030, and the red marks. A wider view of each opening, and a raking-light or reversed
image of strip 1, would help.
